_label: synthetic: hand-written documents and relevance judgements for benchmarking only; not real data

documents.title: Feeding a sourdough starter
documents.text: A sourdough starter needs feeding with equal parts flour and water every twelve hours at room temperature. A bubbly, doubled starter is ready to leaven bread.

documents.title: Shaping and proofing dough
documents.text: After bulk fermentation, shape the loaf and let it proof in a floured banneton. A cold overnight proof in the refrigerator develops a tangy flavor.

documents.title: Scoring and baking crusty loaves
documents.text: Score the loaf with a razor blade and bake in a preheated Dutch oven. Trapped steam gives the crust a crackling, golden finish.

documents.title: Why is my bread dense
documents.text: A dense crumb usually means an underactive starter or insufficient fermentation time. Warmer kitchens speed up rising while cold ones slow it.

documents.title: Hydration in bread recipes
documents.text: Baker's percentage expresses water as a share of flour weight. High hydration doughs of eighty percent produce an open, glossy crumb but are sticky to handle.

documents.title: Grind size for espresso
documents.text: Espresso needs a fine, uniform grind. If shots run too fast and taste sour, grind finer; if they crawl and taste bitter, grind coarser.

documents.title: Dialing in the brew ratio
documents.text: A common espresso recipe uses eighteen grams of coffee to produce thirty-six grams of liquid in about thirty seconds. Adjust the ratio to taste.

documents.title: Milk steaming basics
documents.text: Steam milk until the pitcher is warm to the touch, around sixty degrees Celsius. Microfoam with tiny bubbles is needed for latte art.

documents.title: Descaling your machine
documents.text: Mineral deposits from hard water clog boilers over time. Run a citric acid descaling solution through the machine every three months.

documents.title: Choosing coffee beans
documents.text: Freshly roasted beans within a month of the roast date give the best crema. Store them in an airtight container away from light.

documents.title: Starting tomato seeds indoors
documents.text: Sow tomato seeds indoors six weeks before the last frost. Keep seedlings under grow lights and warm until they have two sets of true leaves.

documents.title: Transplanting seedlings outdoors
documents.text: Harden off seedlings for a week before planting them outside. Bury the stem deep, since buried stems grow extra roots.

documents.title: Watering and mulching tomatoes
documents.text: Water tomatoes deeply at the base, not on the leaves. A layer of straw mulch keeps soil moisture steady and prevents cracked fruit.

documents.title: Blossom end rot
documents.text: Dark sunken patches on the bottom of fruit are blossom end rot, caused by uneven watering and calcium uptake problems. Consistent irrigation prevents it.

documents.title: Staking and pruning vines
documents.text: Indeterminate varieties need tall stakes or cages. Pinch off suckers between the main stem and branches to focus energy on fruit.

documents.title: Building a weekly mileage base
documents.text: Increase weekly running mileage by no more than ten percent to avoid injury. Most plans build a base of easy runs before adding speed work.

documents.title: The long run
documents.text: The long run is the cornerstone of marathon training, peaking at thirty-two kilometers about three weeks before race day. Run it at a conversational pace.

documents.title: Race day fueling
documents.text: Take in thirty to sixty grams of carbohydrate per hour during a marathon with gels or sports drink. Practice your fueling in training to avoid stomach trouble.

documents.title: Tapering before the race
documents.text: Reduce mileage over the final two to three weeks so your legs recover. Keep some intensity but cut volume sharply.

documents.title: Preventing runner's knee
documents.text: Strengthen hips and quadriceps and replace worn shoes every eight hundred kilometers. Pain around the kneecap that worsens on downhills is a warning sign.

documents.title: Level 1 versus Level 2 charging
documents.text: A standard household outlet adds only a few kilometers of range per hour. A Level 2 wall charger at 240 volts fully charges most electric cars overnight.

documents.title: DC fast charging
documents.text: DC fast chargers can restore eighty percent of a battery in thirty minutes. Frequent fast charging may accelerate battery degradation.

documents.title: Installing a home charger
documents.text: A licensed electrician should install a dedicated circuit for a home EV charger. Check that your panel has spare capacity first.

documents.title: Charging off-peak
documents.text: Schedule charging for overnight hours when electricity tariffs are lowest. Most vehicles and wall units support timers in their apps.

documents.title: Cold weather range
documents.text: Battery electric vehicles lose range in freezing temperatures because of cabin heating and battery chemistry. Preconditioning while plugged in recovers some of it.

documents.title: Slow wifi diagnosis
documents.text: Test speed with a wired connection first to separate router problems from internet provider problems. Interference from neighboring networks often slows wireless.

documents.title: Choosing a wifi channel
documents.text: On the 2.4 GHz band only channels 1, 6 and 11 do not overlap. Switch to 5 GHz for less congestion at shorter range.

documents.title: Router placement
documents.text: Place the router centrally and high up, away from microwaves and thick walls. Mesh systems extend coverage to far rooms.

documents.title: DNS problems
documents.text: If pages fail to load but pings succeed, the DNS resolver may be failing. Switch to a public resolver or flush the local DNS cache.

documents.title: Securing your router
documents.text: Change the default admin password, enable WPA3 encryption, and keep router firmware updated. Disable remote administration unless you need it.

documents.title: The fifty thirty twenty rule
documents.text: Allocate fifty percent of take-home pay to needs, thirty percent to wants, and twenty percent to savings and debt repayment. Adjust the shares to your situation.

documents.title: Building an emergency fund
documents.text: Aim to save three to six months of essential expenses in an easily accessible account. Automate a transfer each payday.

documents.title: Paying off credit card debt
documents.text: The avalanche method pays the highest interest rate card first, saving the most money. The snowball method clears the smallest balance first for motivation.

documents.title: Tracking monthly expenses
documents.text: Categorize every transaction for a month to find spending leaks. Subscriptions you forgot about are a common culprit.

documents.title: Sinking funds
documents.text: A sinking fund sets aside a small amount monthly for a predictable large expense such as car repairs or holidays. It prevents irregular costs from derailing your budget.

documents.title: Overwatering signs
documents.text: Yellowing lower leaves and soggy soil indicate overwatering. Let the top few centimeters of soil dry out between waterings and make sure pots drain.

documents.title: Light requirements
documents.text: Succulents need bright direct light while ferns prefer shade. Leggy, stretched growth means the plant is not getting enough light.

documents.title: Repotting houseplants
documents.text: Repot when roots circle the bottom of the pot or emerge from drainage holes. Choose a container only one size larger.

documents.title: Pests on indoor plants
documents.text: Spider mites leave fine webbing and speckled leaves. Wipe leaves with soapy water or use neem oil to control fungus gnats and mites.

documents.title: Humidity for tropical plants
documents.text: Tropical foliage plants such as calatheas want humidity above fifty percent. Group plants together or use a pebble tray to raise moisture in dry rooms.

documents.title: Lubricating the chain
documents.text: Wipe the chain clean and apply a drop of lubricant to each link. A dry or squeaky drivetrain wears out the cassette and chainrings faster.

documents.title: Fixing a flat tire
documents.text: Remove the wheel, pry off the tire with levers, and replace the punctured inner tube. Check inside the tire for the thorn or glass before reinflating.

documents.title: Adjusting brakes
documents.text: If the brake lever pulls to the handlebar, tighten the cable barrel adjuster. Replace pads when the wear grooves disappear.

documents.title: Tire pressure
documents.text: Road tires run at higher pressure than mountain bike tires. Lower pressure improves grip and comfort on rough surfaces.

documents.title: Indexing the gears
documents.text: Poor shifting is usually fixed by turning the barrel adjuster on the rear derailleur a quarter turn at a time. Check that the derailleur hanger is straight.

documents.title: A consistent sleep schedule
documents.text: Going to bed and waking at the same time every day, even on weekends, stabilizes your circadian rhythm. Irregular schedules cause grogginess.

documents.title: Screens before bed
documents.text: Blue light from phones suppresses melatonin. Stop using screens an hour before bed or enable a night mode.

documents.title: Bedroom environment
documents.text: A cool, dark, quiet bedroom improves sleep quality. Around eighteen degrees Celsius is comfortable for most people.

documents.title: Caffeine and sleep
documents.text: Caffeine has a half-life of about five hours, so an afternoon coffee can disrupt falling asleep at night. Avoid it after early afternoon.

documents.title: Handling insomnia
documents.text: If you cannot fall asleep after twenty minutes, get up and do something calm in dim light. Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia is the first-line treatment.

documents.title: Using a password manager
documents.text: A password manager generates and stores unique long passwords so you only remember one master passphrase. It eliminates password reuse across sites.

documents.title: Two-factor authentication
documents.text: Enable two-factor authentication with an authenticator app or hardware key. SMS codes are weaker because of SIM swapping attacks.

documents.title: Recognizing phishing
documents.text: Phishing emails create urgency and link to lookalike domains. Hover over links and never enter credentials after clicking an email link.

documents.title: Checking for breaches
documents.text: Breach notification databases tell you if your email appeared in a leak. Change passwords for affected accounts immediately.

documents.title: Passphrases versus complexity
documents.text: Long passphrases of four random words are easier to remember and harder to crack than short strings with symbols. Length matters more than complexity.

documents.title: How photovoltaic panels work
documents.text: Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight into direct current electricity. An inverter converts it to alternating current for household use.

documents.title: Sizing a rooftop system
documents.text: Estimate your annual electricity consumption and divide by local sun hours to size the array in kilowatts. South-facing roofs in the northern hemisphere produce the most.

documents.title: Net metering
documents.text: Net metering credits you for surplus power exported to the grid. Policies and credit rates vary by utility and region.

documents.title: Home battery storage
documents.text: A home battery stores midday solar surplus for evening use and provides backup during outages. Payback depends on tariffs and incentives.

documents.title: Panel maintenance
documents.text: Panels need little upkeep beyond occasional rinsing of dust and bird droppings. Monitor output to catch shading or inverter faults.
